acceptanceCriteria: `script/check-install-lifecycle.sh` runs with the published 0.7.0 archive as `CORVINT_LIFECYCLE_BINARY` and the 0.8.0 candidate as the upgrade, and `upgrade-b` passes under the amended SOP-V0-003 (`packet=identical|changed` against the upgrade's own cold-index packet) on every host tuple V1-0016 keeps as supported; each run is recorded in BUILD-LOG with the archive digests.

docs/specs/stable-operations-v0.md records the 0.6.0 to 0.7.0 `upgrade-b` failure under the 0341 rule as a closed historical finding and the 0.7.0 to 0.8.0 run as the current N-1 evidence; the 1.0 spec's N-1 readability claim (PRS-V1-002) cites it.
A rollback run (0.8.0 back to 0.7.0) keeps byte identity or records the exact packet difference; no run is reported PASS from a stale receipt.
body: Filed on 2026-09-23 from owner answer 19 of the 1.0 scope questions (decision 0373): fix the 0.7.0 N-1 upgrade failure in 0.8 rather than accept it as a documented limitation. The 0.6.0 (build 90) to 0.7.0 upgrade failed `upgrade-b` under the decision 0341 byte-identity rule because 0.7.0 adds `coverage.governance_refused` and evidence `trust` (docs/specs/stable-operations-v0.md:55, BUILD-LOG 2026-09-23 V1-0089 entry); decision 0360 amended SOP-V0-003 and the N-1 run passes with `packet=changed` on darwin arm64, linux arm64 (container) and darwin amd64 (Rosetta 2), but the published 0.7.0 archive itself was never qualified as the N-1 base for a later release. 0.8 must retain that run on the supported tuples so the 1.0 N-1 promise has current evidence.
title: ops: qualify the 0.7.0 to 0.8.0 N-1 upgrade (`upgrade-b`) under the amended SOP-V0-003 on the supported host tuples
